hero.lead: A nation of 86 million bridging Europe and Asia, where the World Bank approved $2 billion in March 2026 for rail across the Istanbul Strait and public debt stood at 23.7% of GDP in 2025.

capital.heading: The middle corridor, built on rail and on earthquake recovery.

register.name: Ten-year sustainable bond in US dollars
register.detail: Ministry of Treasury and Finance · announced 23 September 2026 · proceeds received 30 September 2026 · due 30 January 2037 · coupon 7.500% · yield 7.650% · orders more than three times the issue size from over 100 accounts
register.note: The Treasury’s second ESG bond in international markets, and its first since 2023
register.text: A dollar ESG bond (Sustainable) of the Republic of Türkiye, due 2037. The Treasury’s release names no eligible project categories, so the bond is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Seven-year green bond in US dollars
register.detail: Ministry of Treasury and Finance · announced 5 April 2023 · issue date 13 April 2023 · due 13 July 2030 · coupon 9.125% · issue price 99.117% · net proceeds $2.476bn
register.note: The first green bond of the Republic of Türkiye; an older instrument, due 2030
register.text: The inaugural green bond of the Republic of Türkiye, registered with the US SEC. In the Treasury’s 2024 allocation report, 12.83% of the allocation went to sustainable water and wastewater management, with more than 1.4 million people to gain improved sanitation, which carries the shelter and water standards; 56.39% went to clean transportation.

register.name: University Hospital Resilience Project
register.detail: World Bank · approved 30 October 2026 · co-financed with $347 million from the AIIB · total $1.047 billion
register.note: Nine university hospital buildings with 4,021 beds
register.text: Builds nine modern, disaster-resilient university hospital buildings in Ağrı, Adana, Erzurum, İzmir, Kahramanmaraş, Kastamonu, Kayseri, Konya and Samsun, with 4,021 beds. It is expected to improve access to tertiary health services for an estimated 3.14 million people a year, which carries the health standard.

register.name: Transforming Industry with Technology (TransformIndustry)
register.detail: World Bank · approved 27 October 2026 · long-term financing through participating financial institutions
register.note: Financing for 280 firms; about 102,000 more and better-paid jobs expected
register.text: Supports small and medium-size manufacturers in adopting digital and green technology, with financing for 280 firms and help for about 400 firms to prepare transformation plans. It is expected to generate about 102,000 more and better-paid jobs and promotes the participation of women-owned and women-led businesses, which carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: Agrifood Sector Transformation for Rural Jobs and Growth (TARGET)
register.detail: World Bank Group · approved 24 September 2026 · P514478
register.note: Expected to benefit about 225,000 farmers
register.text: Strengthens agrifood value chains to bring investment, markets and rural jobs, including in less developed regions and for women and youth. It is expected to benefit about 225,000 farmers, which carries the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Earthquake recovery and resilient housing, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank · approved 30 June 2026 · with €150 million of co-financing from the AFD · total €400 million · P180849, US$291 million
register.note: 3,000 more rural homes for families still living in temporary shelters
register.text: An additional loan to the Türkiye Earthquake Recovery and Reconstruction Project, first approved in June 2023. It finances 3,000 additional rural homes for families still living in temporary shelters, homes for an additional 10,470 people in the earthquake-affected areas, which carries the shelter standard.

register.name: Distributed energy market transition, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank · approved 15 June 2026 · two €200 million IBRD loans to TKYB and TSKB, guaranteed by the Republic of Türkiye · US$468.4 million equivalent
register.note: 1,579 MW of renewable capacity enabled, up from 963 MW, and 392 MWh of battery storage
register.text: Additional financing for the distributed energy program approved in 2024, part of the Europe and Central Asia Renewable Energy Scale-up (ECARES) Program, now extended to onshore wind, new types of distributed solar and battery storage, which carries the energy standard.

register.name: Green and Future Cities Project
register.detail: World Bank Group · approved, announced 5 June 2026 · through İller Bankası (ILBANK) with the guarantee of the Republic of Türkiye · Antalya and Konya · US$219.4 million
register.note: Water supply, wastewater treatment and sanitation, with tramlines and energy efficiency
register.text: A loan to modernise Antalya and Konya, implemented through İller Bankası. It finances upgrades to water supply, wastewater treatment and sanitation infrastructure, which carry the water and shelter standards, alongside public transport, energy efficiency and climate adaptation.

register.name: Rail connectivity across the Istanbul Strait
register.detail: World Bank · Approved March 2026
register.text: Strengthens rail links between Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus.

register.name: Education for tomorrow’s careers
register.detail: World Bank · December 2025
register.text: Equips students and teachers for the careers ahead.

register.name: Access to Finance for Jobs and Growth (FINGROW)
register.detail: World Bank · approved by the Board 15 December 2025 · IBRD guarantee (US$867.8 million equivalent) · backs a 10-year facility of up to €1.5 billion from international lenders to VakıfBank
register.note: About 30,000 MSMEs, 15,000 of them women-led; up to 800,000 jobs
register.text: An IBRD guarantee that mobilises up to €1.5 billion of commercial financing for micro, small and medium enterprises through VakıfBank, with a focus on women and youth and on underdeveloped and disaster-affected regions. It is expected to reach about 30,000 firms, including 15,000 women-led and 1,000 youth-led firms, which carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: Eastern Türkiye Middle Corridor Railway
register.detail: IBRD · Approved 5 December 2024
register.text: Rail on the Middle Corridor to the Caucasus and Central Asia.

register.name: Small Industrial Estates Reconstruction
register.detail: IBRD · Approved 29 July 2024
register.text: Rebuilds industrial estates in the earthquake region.

register.name: Distributed energy market transition (ECARES)
register.detail: IBRD · Approved 28 March 2024
register.text: Rooftop and distributed renewable power.

register.name: Green Export Project
register.detail: IBRD · Approved 22 February 2024
register.text: Helps exporters meet green standards in their markets.

register.name: Türk Eximbank sustainable infrastructure and economic resilience loans
register.detail: AIIB · signed 13 November 2026, Antalya · two sovereign-backed loans: $100 million for sustainable infrastructure and $200 million for economic resilience
register.note: A portion is earmarked for borrowers in the 11 provinces affected by the 2023 earthquakes
register.text: Two loans to Türk Eximbank, Türkiye’s official export credit agency. One gives private firms long-term finance for renewable energy, energy storage, energy efficiency, clean mobility and climate adaptation; the other gives liquidity to businesses, including small and medium-sized enterprises, which carries the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Water Efficiency and Climate Resilience for Results
register.detail: AIIB · loan agreement signed, announced 24 April 2026 · results-based financing program · P001015
register.note: Nearly 45,000 hectares and more than 540,000 people
register.text: A results-based program with the Republic of Türkiye that upgrades irrigation with efficient pipelines and volumetric flow meters and strengthens flood risk management across priority river basins. It is expected to improve water management across nearly 45,000 hectares and benefit more than 540,000 people; it serves farming and flood protection, which carries the food standard, rather than drinking water.

register.name: ISMEP V, seismic risk mitigation for public facilities
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 13 June 2025 · borrower: Government
register.note: Includes the reconstruction of two critical public hospitals in Istanbul
register.text: Part-finances earthquake preparedness in Istanbul, with a focus on the reconstruction of two critical public hospitals. Its beneficiaries are the 16 million inhabitants of Istanbul, including migrants and refugees, which carries the health standard.

register.name: DenizLeasing green economy financing (GEFF III)
register.detail: EBRD · announced during COP31 in Antalya, November 2026 · up to €70.5 million from the EBRD and up to €4.5 million of concessional funding from the CIF Clean Technology Fund
register.note: At least 30% for businesses in the regions hit by the 2023 earthquakes
register.text: A new EBRD loan to Deniz Finansal Kiralama under the Türkiye Green Economy Financing Facility III, for investments in energy and resource efficiency, renewable energy and climate resilience. At least 30 per cent goes to businesses in the earthquake regions, and DenizLeasing aims to finance more women-led businesses, which carries the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Ak Lease green economy financing (GEFF III)
register.detail: EBRD · 16 November 2026 · €47.4 million from the EBRD and €2.6 million of concessional financing from TaiwanICDF
register.note: At least 30% for new leases in the regions affected by the 2023 earthquakes
register.text: An EBRD loan to Ak Lease under the €1 billion Türkiye Green Economy Financing Facility III, for private companies investing in energy and resource efficiency and renewable energy. At least 30 per cent is earmarked for new leases in the earthquake regions, which carries the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: DenizBank women, youth and green finance package
register.detail: EBRD · 12 November 2026 · up to €50 million under Women in Business II · up to €50 million under Youth in Business · up to €75 million under GEFF III (€70.5 million EBRD, €4.5 million Clean Technology Fund)
register.note: Women and youth lending supported by the Türkiye Credit Guarantee Fund
register.text: Longer-term loans through DenizBank to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises owned or led by women and to firms led by young entrepreneurs, including in the earthquake-affected regions, with green finance for businesses and individuals. At least 30 per cent of the green finance is earmarked for new loans in the earthquake regions, which carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: İş Leasing green investment and earthquake recovery (GEFF III)
register.detail: EBRD · 23 October 2026 · financing package of up to €100 million
register.note: At least 30% for the regions affected by the 2023 earthquakes
register.text: An EBRD package to İş Finansal Kiralama under the Türkiye Green Economy Financing Facility III, for energy and resource efficiency, renewable energy and climate resilience. At least 30 per cent goes to the earthquake regions, and it seeks to broaden women’s access to green finance, which carries the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: TEB lending to women-led small businesses
register.detail: EBRD · 24 September 2026 · under the €600 million Türkiye Women in Business II programme
register.note: At least 70% of the lending to women-led MSMEs outside major cities
register.text: An EBRD loan to Türk Ekonomi Bankası for women-owned and women-led micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, with at least 70 per cent of the lending outside the major cities and 35 per cent to new clients, which carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: DenizBank green bond
register.detail: AIIB · nonsovereign · approved 16 December 2025 · five-year amortizing green bond, private placement · investment announced 10 September 2026
register.note: Proceeds for climate mitigation projects of corporate, commercial and SME borrowers
register.text: An AIIB investment in a five-year green bond of DenizBank. Its proceeds fund climate mitigation projects in renewable energy, energy efficiency, clean transportation and sustainable water and wastewater management, which carries the energy and water standards.

register.name: Akbank digital gender bond
register.detail: IFC · 3 December 2025 · Digitally Native Note, issued and settled the same day
register.note: Described by the IFC as the world’s first digitally issued gender bond
register.text: An IFC investment in a digitally issued gender bond of Akbank, with all proceeds going to projects that expand financing for women-owned small and medium enterprises, which carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: TEB subordinated loan for climate and women-owned businesses
register.detail: IFC · 8 May 2024 · up to €100 million of Tier-2 subordinated debt
register.text: IFC financing to Türk Ekonomi Bankası to lend to small and medium enterprises for climate mitigation and adaptation projects, to women-owned businesses and to agribusinesses, which carries the livelihood standard.
register.note: For small and medium enterprises, women-owned businesses and agribusinesses

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 21% are under fifteen: a large, young workforce at the meeting point of Europe and Asia.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Half the land in farming: hazelnuts, figs, apricots and grain for the world.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: A third of the power from water, wind and sun, and room for much more.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2020
items.text: Istanbul, Cappadocia and the Aegean coast: visitors from every continent.

items.name: Fazla
items.text: An Istanbul waste-management company and certified B Corporation that uses technology to reduce waste and to create the highest environmental, social and economic value out of surplus food and goods, including donations to food banks and charities.

items.name: Otsimo
items.text: A subscription app that gives neurodiverse children, including children with autism, cognitive and behavioural education and speech therapy, and that has been used free of charge in autism classrooms in cities across Türkiye.

items.name: b-fit
items.text: A national chain of women-only gyms franchised only to women entrepreneurs, which in 19 years has given more than 5,000 women the chance to become entrepreneurs.

items.name: Turkish Grameen Microfinance Program
items.text: A non-profit microfinance organisation that lends to women, especially in rural areas not served by formal financial institutions; on Kiva, 99.96% of its loans go to women and the average loan is $310.

items.name: Nahıl
items.text: The economic enterprise of the Kadın Emeğini Değerlendirme Vakfı (KEDV), which sells the products of women’s cooperatives and in December 2025 brought products from 101 women’s cooperatives in 44 provinces to Istanbul.

coverage.gap_text: Of people in Türkiye lack safely managed sanitation.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: No FAO measure of food insecurity is published for Türkiye

guarantees.name: Water
guarantees.note: Basic drinking water; safely managed water is not measured (lenient)

guarantees.name: Shelter
guarantees.note: Safely managed sanitation; 14.1% of city dwellers live in slums

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: 98% cook with clean fuels and technology; 100% have electricity

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 81.5% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above the national poverty line; 13% live below it
